claims.text: High-temperature shockwave stabilization of high-entropy nanoalloys will improve their structural stability relative to otherwise comparable untreated nanoalloys.
High-temperature shockwave stabilization of high-entropy nanoalloys will improve their chemical stability relative to otherwise comparable untreated nanoalloys.
High-temperature shockwave stabilization induces single-atom evolution in the primary particles.
High-temperature shockwave stabilization causes oxygen to leave the primary particles.
Single-atom evolution and oxygen loss from primary particles produce improved structural stability.
Single-atom evolution and oxygen loss from primary particles produce improved chemical stability.
The predicted stabilization should hold over an application-temperature range of 60–120 °C.
The exact mechanism and effects of high-temperature shockwave stabilization on high-entropy nanoalloys are not fully understood.
Failure of the treated nanoalloys to show improved structural and chemical stability relative to untreated controls would falsify the hypothesis.
